2026-11-17.title: Briefed · Tue, Nov 17: Gas hits $3.78, lowest since March
2026-11-17.description: Gas falls to $3.78 a gallon, its lowest since March. Plus: a nationwide emergency alert test at 2:20 p.m. ET on TV and radio only (phones won't get it), Nvidia reports earnings tonight after the Nasdaq's slide, Iran fires drones at a U.S. radar site in Bahrain, California sues OpenAI over rogue AI agents, and Trump meets Quad leaders in Manila ahead of talks with Xi and Putin. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-17/

2026-11-18.title: Briefed · Wed, Nov 18: Two outages in four days, FAA says no cyberattack

2026-11-19.title: Briefed · Thu, Nov 19: Four-point peace declaration, no Ukraine ceasefire
2026-11-19.description: President Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held their first three-way meeting in Shenzhen and a four-point declaration on peace was published by Chinese and Russian state media; the Associated Press says China and Russia say the United States agreed, and no Ukraine ceasefire was announced. Plus: AAA projects 81.5 million Thanksgiving travelers, with booked domestic fares averaging $800, up 17%; Anthropic set its I.P.O. share price at $83 and raised $81.3 billion, with ANT due to start trading today after 9:30 a.m. Eastern; House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, 251-11; Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point December rate increase may be needed; and Target reported sales up 7.1% and is offering a $30 Thanksgiving meal for six. Sources: BBC, The Guardian, AP, AAA, Anthropic, CNBC, NBC, NPR, ABC, Target, Fox Business. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-19/

2026-11-20.title: Briefed · Fri, Nov 20: Dow closes under 50,000 as AI selloff deepens
2026-11-20.description: The Dow fell 1,101 points to 49,097, its first close under 50,000 since June, as the AI selloff deepened; the S&P 500 fell for a sixth straight day, and Anthropic closed its first day of trading at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 offer price. Plus: President Trump says a decision on new large-scale strikes on Iran can wait until after the new year ("We've got time"); Vladimir Putin says Russia will make no agreements after Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge, as Russia attacks Kyiv; the Senate passes a bipartisan energy permitting bill, 62-33, that would make data centers pay for the power they use; and the Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo has died. Sources: CNBC, AP, Yahoo Finance, Reuters, Axios, CBS News, AFP, The Guardian, Politico, NPR, Roll Call, Cincinnati Zoo, BBC. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-20/

2026-11-21.title: Briefed · Sat, Nov 21: St. Johns River hits a 73-year flood record
2026-11-21.description: The St. Johns River near Cocoa, Florida, was forecast to crest at 18.8 feet on Saturday, a 73-year record, after rain that topped 28 inches in some areas; Rockledge still has a voluntary evacuation, and officials say flooding could last two to three months, through Thanksgiving. Plus: the Farm Bureau says a Thanksgiving dinner for 10 now costs $58.63, or $5.86 a person, up 6%, the first increase since 2022, with a 16-pound turkey averaging $23.68, up 10%; the Dow fell 950 points Friday to 48,147 and the S&P 500 fell 3.7%, both closing more than 10% below their records, while Nvidia fell 14% after Reuters, citing sources, said SEC staff are examining possible accounting issues; Polish officials say a Russian cruise missile entered Polish airspace Friday, and a strike on Zelenskyy's hometown, Kryvyi Rih, killed a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman and wounded 60 people; President Trump said U.S. companies that build AI data centers abroad will face a "tremendous tax," with no rate given, and a second federal judge blocked his planned 250-foot memorial arch; and NASA says Voyager 1 has reached one light-day from Earth, about 16.1 billion miles. Sources: AP, National Weather Service, AccuWeather, Farm Bureau, Axios, Washington Post, CNBC, Reuters, Yahoo Finance, BBC, Courthouse News, NASA, Space.com. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-21/

2026-11-22.title: Briefed · Sun, Nov 22: 'El Chapo Isidro,' an FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive, is captured
2026-11-22.description: One of the FBI's Ten Most Wanted, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," was captured Friday in Guasave, Sinaloa, with U.S. help; he faced a $5 million American reward, a firefight left at least 11 dead, including 4 Mexican soldiers, and FBI Director Kash Patel said he is the 11th Ten Most Wanted fugitive taken under this administration. The United States wants him extradited. Plus: forecasters say San Francisco's tide is expected to reach 8.8 feet Wednesday, above the 8.66-foot record from 1983, a figure that includes storm surge, and Mayor Daniel Lurie says skip nonessential travel Monday afternoon through Wednesday, with a storm hitting the East Coast today and a major Northeast storm possible on Thanksgiving; the FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center, the database police use for warrants and background checks, according to people briefed on the matter, and it is not known who did it or whether data was taken or changed; President Trump signed an order Friday requiring federal contractors to notify the White House of congressional requests about their executive-branch work and to follow instructions to withhold anything it deems covered by executive privilege, with the White House saying the order protects confidential and national-security information; a child in Virginia, age 4 or younger, has died with measles, the state's first measles-associated death since 1978, officials said, without saying whether the child had other health conditions, while states have reported at least 12 measles-associated deaths this year and the CDC lists 6; and three tankers were struck near the Strait of Hormuz over about 15 hours, a British maritime agency reported, with no casualties reported, in attacks suspected to be Iranian. Sources: Department of Justice, NPR, Associated Press, ABC News, Weather.com, NOAA, NBC Bay Area, NBC News, BBC, Reuters, CNBC, the White House, Politico, Virginia Department of Health, WJLA, CDC, KFF, Al Jazeera. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-22/

2026-11-23.title: Briefed · Mon, Nov 23: More than 1,600 Delta flights were delayed Sunday before Thanksgiving
2026-11-23.description: More than 1,600 Delta flights were delayed Sunday after a weight-and-balance system went down; about 49 percent of Delta's Sunday flights were more than 15 minutes late, 202 flights were canceled, most of the delays were at Atlanta, Delta said the system was later restored and that the outage was not a hack, and the FAA said the delays were not related to its air-traffic systems. Plus: the Army plans to detonate nearly 5 tons of deteriorating lead azide on Wednesday at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, after delays for weather and safety measures, with the Justice Department saying the Army can proceed under an emergency exemption even though an appeals court has paused the environmental permit, and environmental groups warning of lead dust; ICE officers detained a father and daughter, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Mejia, at Sea-Tac Airport on Saturday as they boarded an Alaska Airlines flight to Los Angeles for a family baptism, their lawyer said, and the agency said they had overstayed visas and that Mejia threw hot coffee, while the lawyer and a passenger said it spilled, and the airline said it got no advance notice; Democrats have reached at least 258 House seats, their largest majority since 1992, after Chuck Hubbard defeated Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, who conceded Sunday after a recount, with Hubbard leading by 330 votes out of nearly 300,000 ballots, and four House races still outstanding, including two Louisiana runoffs in December; and rural colleges are shrinking as fewer kids go to college, with Pennsylvania's college-going rate falling from 70 percent in 2009 to 58 percent in 2024 according to the state system, high-school graduating classes also set to decline, including about 17 percent in Pennsylvania by 2041, suburban West Chester growing while rural campuses including PennWest and Lock Haven have shrunk, and Mansfield down from 3,569 students in 2009 to 1,013 this fall, with a plan due December 8 to wind the campus down by June 30, 2028, pending a board vote. Sources: ABC News, CBS News, Associated Press, U.S. Army, Iowa Public Radio, NBC News, BBC, Roll Call, Christian Science Monitor, Philadelphia Inquirer, PASSHE, WICHE. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-23/

2026-11-24.title: Briefed · Tue, Nov 24: Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO; stock closed up 31.5%
2026-11-24.description: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, and the stock closed up 31.5 percent, at $165.05; President Trump said he was involved, and the board said it got input from senior U.S. officials and sees no national security risk, but its investigation will continue. Plus: the national average for a gallon of regular gas has fallen to $3.61, down 17 cents in a week, as Thanksgiving travel gets underway, about 68 cents below a month ago but still about 55 cents higher than a year ago; an unvaccinated resident of Centre County, Pennsylvania, has died with measles, the state's ninth measles-associated death this year, officials released no other details citing privacy law, earlier Pennsylvania deaths included people in cancer treatment and people with severe respiratory conditions, state health departments have now reported thirteen such deaths, and the CDC dashboard still lists six; Social Security benefits will rise 3.6 percent in 2027, lifting the average retired worker's check to about $2,170 a month, while the standard Medicare Part B premium is going up $6.50, to $209.40, usually taken from the benefit, so on a $1,000 check that hike eats 18 percent of the raise, and September inflation was 3.7 percent; a U.S.-led Board of Peace report to the U.N. Security Council warns the Gaza ceasefire could collapse without full implementation, an adviser says Israel is stalling and the board could hand Gaza back to the U.N., Israel says Hamas has not handed over a single weapon, and hospital officials said at least eight people were killed in strikes overnight — why that matters here: this is President Trump's 20-point plan, and a collapse would test U.S. credibility in the region; and President Zelenskyy says that if there is no acceptable peace deal by year's end, he will turn to the new Democratic-controlled Congress for more U.S. military aid and tougher sanctions on Russia — why that matters here: next year's aid and sanctions decisions would go through the new Congress. Sources: Nvidia, CNBC, The Motley Fool, Investing.com, AAA, Fortune, Pennsylvania Department of Health, The Philadelphia Inquirer, CBS News, Social Security Administration, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Bureau of Labor Statistics, Associated Press, The Times of Israel, Ynet, Al-Monitor, Bloomberg. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-24/

2026-11-25.title: Briefed · Wed, Nov 25: U.S. foreign-aid agency posts 248 files on Google, YouTube, and Meta
2026-11-25.description: Two hundred forty-eight files went up on the U.S. foreign-aid agency's own homepage, including a 2022 note that described more than 2,500 websites already built into 13 ad companies' systems. The files cover work with Google, YouTube, and Meta. The administration says it posted them for accountability. Plus: New York's mayor wants to push the Rikers Island closing date from 2027 to 2032, the City Council still has to change the law, four borough jails are budgeted at $11.47 billion, the plan needs the jail population to fall from about 6,600 to no more than 4,100, the officers' union opposes it, and Staten Island council members say their borough is left without a jail; the Army is set this morning to detonate more than 9,700 pounds of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, officials say it has crystallized in 68 drums and is too sensitive to move, and FEMA has asked residents in a five-mile area southwest of the plant to relocate for the blast; the TSA expects to screen 17.6 million air travelers this Thanksgiving week, a bit below last year, the FAA is forecasting about 418,000 flights over nine days, and storms and king tides are a risk on both coasts; Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009, has asked a federal court to delay his execution by firing squad, it would be the first U.S. military execution since 1961, a hearing is set for this afternoon, and the execution had been scheduled for December 3; officials say hackers broke into an unclassified CIA system used for open-source intelligence, they say no classified networks were touched and that the issue has been resolved, and a possible China link has not been confirmed; and U.S. Marshals are searching for Ronald Rutledge, 45, accused of firing a rifle at deputies in Stevens County, Washington, no deputies were injured, they're offering up to $3,500 for information leading to his arrest, and he was still at large this morning. Sources: USAID.gov, The Boston Report, NYC Mayor's Office, Close Rikers Strategic Plan, New York City Council, SILive, U.S. Army, Iowa Homeland Security, TSA, FAA, Reuters, CourtListener, Associated Press, ABC News, The Washington Post, Nextgov, U.S. Marshals Service, The Spokesman-Review, KIRO 7. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-25/

2026-11-26.title: Briefed · Thu, Nov 26: Nor'easter pushes Macy's parade to Saturday for the first time ever
2026-11-26.description: A nor'easter has pushed Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade to Saturday morning at 8:30, the first time weather has ever postponed it. New York City expects gusts of 60 to 65 miles an hour this afternoon, and New Jersey and parts of New York are under states of emergency. More than 360 U.S. flights were canceled by this morning. Forecasters expect a dry Saturday. Plus: the U.S. Trade Representative, Jamieson Greer, has proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, including China, the European Union, Japan, and India; the proposed rates go up to 35% for Vietnam, up to 25% for India, and up to 20% for China, the E.U. would face 15%, and Japan up to 15%; none of it takes effect yet, public comments are due January 5, and hearings start January 25; the Fed's preferred inflation gauge rose to 3.8% in October from a year earlier, up from 3.7% in September, core inflation, which leaves out food and energy, was 3.3%, and CNBC reports markets have now fully priced in a quarter-point rate hike when the Federal Reserve meets December 8 and 9; and a federal judge in Washington has blocked President Trump's second birthright-citizenship order for a certified class of people it would affect, Judge Christopher Cooper wrote that the Citizenship Clause promises citizenship to practically all children born in the United States, the order targeted children of some foreign-government workers, children born through surrogacy to foreign parents, and children of suspected gang members, and the White House called it a ruling from an activist judge. Sources: NYC Mayor's Office, New Jersey Governor's Office, NBC News, ABC News, Associated Press, U.S. Trade Representative, Reuters, NPR, Bureau of Economic Analysis, CNBC, CourtListener, Bloomberg Law, Fox News. Full edition and sources: ljiindustries.com/briefed/2026-11-26/
